title: The Thiele Machine: A Computational Model with Explicit Structural Cost
description:
I didn't invent a machine. I found one. That is my conviction. The Thiele Machine is an abstract model of computation, a machine the way Turing's is: a state, a step rule, a record that only goes up, a toll that the step raising the record must pay, and a window saying what an observer sees. It computes nothing a Turing machine can't. What it adds is a place, enforced by the step itself, for what a computation established and what establishing it cost. This work is an argument, made with that model, that an account of computation should carry that axis.

Proved in Coq, with every premise printed: anything that follows the toll pays to get from uncertified to certified. On a finite machine whose certificate is never taken back, the certifying step merges states, so the toll follows from pricing merges, with Landauer's principle as a named premise; a measurement that forgets nothing can be priced at zero. A window that shows a certifying step and a quiet one alike cannot price certification exactly. Over any base machine, an honest permanent record is a latch on an event; which event deserves it is a conjecture.

Two machines are witnesses. A minimal two-counter machine with CHECK, COMMIT and CERTIFY, where every raised certificate went through a passing check of exactly that claim; it is Thiele-complete, and a universal Thiele machine built on it runs any of its programs as a guest with the guest's record and toll enforced by the host's own step. And a 51-opcode VM with an extracted runner and a Kami/Bluespec/Verilog hardware development, a test bench that prices commitments without checking that they were earned; its CPU implements 47 of the 51 opcodes with 32-bit words and has run on no physical board.

The repository contains the Coq kernel and proofs, the hardware development, the monograph (PDF and plain text), and the mathematical specification. The assumption receipt lists every statement and what it depends on: none depend on project-local or third-party axioms, only on five named standard-library constants. Physical and foundational readings are stated as premises or conjectures, never as results.
